title: Master vs. master
description: With little time or money, George Lucas' visual effects wizards struggled mightily to achieve unprecedented images. Theories began to surface that these specialists lacked discipline, forcing the director to intervene frequently as insurance that they were on schedule for a summer '77 release. With hundreds of uncompleted shots to complete, ILM was forced to finish a year's work in only six months. Lucas inspired his team by editing together aerial dogfights from old war movies, which enhanced the pacing of action sequences. In the end, ILM's tired technicians were vindicated when Star Wars won an Oscar for Best Visual effects, beating out Close Encounters of the Third Kind.
